title: Andrej Karpathy on AI coding transformation at Sequoia AI Ascent 2026
description: At Sequoia AI Ascent 2026, Andrej Karpathy discussed how dramatically programming has changed in the last 2 months. Last year he coined 'vibe coding', but this year he expressed feeling 'never felt more behind as a programmer'. Karpathy shared extensive experience coding with Claude over the past few weeks and how coding workflows have fundamentally transformed, describing it as 'hard to communicate how much programming has changed'. The shift is not gradual but significant, with potential 10x productivity gains by combining new AI capabilities.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: The new GPT-5.6 family: Luna, Terra, Sol
description: OpenAI's latest flagship model hit general availability, coming in three sizes: Luna, Terra, and Sol (from smallest to largest). This represents a new family of models from OpenAI with multiple size options.
author: Simon Willison

title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
description: Following Muse Spark in April, Meta released Muse Spark 1.1 - the first Spark model to offer an API. Meta claims significant improvements in agentic tool calling and computer use. The model includes interesting features like 'Attractor States in Self-Conversation' where having two copies of the model talk to each other results in existential statements.
author: Simon Willison

title: Popular open source AI developer tool Ollama raises $65M, grows to nearly 9M users
description: Ollama raised a $65M Series B led by Theory Ventures, following a previous $15M Series A led by Benchmark. The tool helps developers run open-weight AI models on their PCs in minutes. With 176,000 GitHub stars and 17,000 forks, Ollama is used by over 8.9M developers monthly and sits in 85% of Fortune 500. Founders previously built Docker Desktop. The tipping point came when OpenClaw became hot around January 2026, as larger open models became capable of agentic tasks like coding.
author: Julie Bort (TechCrunch)

title: Rewriting Bun in Rust
description: Jarred Sumner completed a sophisticated Zig to Rust rewrite of Bun using coding agents powered by frontier models. The project cost approximately $165,000 in API tokens (5.9B input, 690M output, 72B cached reads). The rewrite addressed memory management bugs (use-after-free, double-free, forgot to free) by leveraging Rust's safety guarantees. A key enabler was the TypeScript test suite acting as a conformance suite, allowing automated agent harness to port the codebase.
author: Simon Willison (via Jarred Sumner)

title: Introducing GPT-Live
description: OpenAI upgraded ChatGPT voice mode with a new model that can delegate harder tasks to GPT-5.5 for web search, deeper reasoning, or complex work. The previous voice mode was based on GPT-4o era model with 2024 knowledge cutoff. During preview, Simon encountered a bug where the model interrupted to laugh at non-jokes, which OpenAI fixed.
author: Simon Willison

title: Kenton Varda declares moratorium against AI-written change descriptions
description: Kenton Varda banned his team from using AI to write PR descriptions, commit messages, and tickets. AI was writing descriptions that outlined code details visible in the code but omitted higher-level framing needed to understand what the code is doing broadly. The AI-generated descriptions were 'worse than useless' for reviewing PRs.
author: Kenton Varda (via Simon Willison)

title: sqlite-utils 4.0, now with database schema migrations
description: Simon released sqlite-utils 4.0, the 124th release and first major version bump since 3.0 in November 2020. New features include database migrations, nested transactions (via db.atomic()), and support for compound foreign keys. The release involved breaking changes with an upgrade guide.
author: Simon Willison

title: tencent/Hy3 - 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model
description: Tencent released Hy3, a 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 21B active parameters and 3.8B MTP layer parameters. It outperforms similar-size models and rivals flagship open-source models with 2-5x parameters. The full model is 598GB on Hugging Face, with FP8 quantized version at 300GB. Context length is 256K. Available free on OpenRouter until July 21st.
author: Simon Willison

title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)
description: Simon used Claude Fable 5 to help complete sqlite-utils 4.0 stable release, documenting the entire process. The work involved implementing compound foreign keys, following SQLite's case-insensitive column name convention, and various improvements. Simon provided detailed breakdown of Fable usage, costs, and the collaborative process with the AI coding agent.
author: Simon Willison

title: Better Models: Worse Tools - Tool schema regression in newer Claude models
description: Armin Ronacher reported that newer Claude models (Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5) sometimes call edit tools with extra, invented fields that don't match the schema. This is worse than older models. The theory is that newer models were trained via RL to better use Claude Code's edit tools (search and replace), which has the unfortunate effect that other coding harnesses like Pi see worse performance. Third-party coding harnesses may need to implement multiple edit tools for different models.
author: Armin Ronacher (via Simon Willison)

title: Building a World Map with only 500 bytes
description: Iwo Kadziela (assisted by Codex) figured out how to generate a credible ASCII world map using 445 bytes of data. The key trick is using deflate compression with fetch() on data: URIs. A neat JavaScript trick demonstrates data URI compression.
author: Iwo Kadziela (via Simon Willison)
